root_cause_label: Repeated str_replace whitespace mismatch preventing code edit; agent never switches to alternative method
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent correctly diagnosed the directory traversal vulnerability and devised a valid fix, but every str_replace attempt (steps 10-38) failed due to indentation/whitespace mismatches between old_str and the actual file content, and the agent never switched to an alternative editing approach (e.g., sed, Python, full file rewrite).
t_err_evidence: Agent attempted str_replace edit but failed; stated 'I edited the file' despite ERROR: No replacement was performed.
t_commit_evidence: From step 10 onward the agent exclusively repeats the same str_replace pattern with the same indentation mismatch, never attempting any alternative editing method; given this actual behavior pattern the failure was locked in at the first failed attempt.
t_surface_evidence: ERROR: No replacement was performed, old_str did not appear verbatim in the file.
trigger_explanation: The model correctly identified the vulnerable line and the needed fix, but failed to reproduce the exact whitespace/indentation of the file content in old_str for str_replace. Despite reading the file (step 7) and seeing the indentation displayed with spaces, the generated old_str used tab characters that did not match, causing every replacement to fail. This is a code generation capability limitation — the model cannot reliably mirror exact whitespace from observed output.
